transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Vector Alliance Channel Director), Aaron Patel (Vector Alliance Head of Partnerships), Sofia Mendes (Vector Alliance Sales Ops)

Summary:
Quick partner co-sell / pipeline review. Went over 6 active opportunities across Retail, FinServ, and Healthcare verticals. Discussed who owns next-touch, whether Redwood or Vector runs the pilot, attribution (co-sell credit), and sequencing for technical benchmarks. Agreed on next steps: share joint GTM deck, schedule two technical intros, and finalize partner registration and referral terms.

Topics:
- Priority deals and owners
- Technical readiness / pilot scope (benchmarks, sample prompt sets, latency/cost targets)
- Commercials: co-sell credit, referral fees, lead routing
- Legal/contracting next steps and SSO/KMS requirements for private deployments

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick intro - I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the Vector Alliance co-sell. Carlos from our SE team is here for the technical pieces.
[00:12] Lena: great thanks Maya, we have Aaron and Sofia here on our side - excited to sync.
[00:18] Carlos: hi all, quick agenda, we'll walk pipeline, technical flags, and commercial asks, then decide owners.
[00:26] Aaron: sounds good, let's dive. First thing, can we get a recap of the six opps you see on the spreadsheet?
[00:33] Maya: yeah uh so top of funnel we have RetailCo (P0), FinCorp (P1), HealthSys (P2), plus three smaller deals, two pilots with mid-market. RetailCo and FinCorp are highest ACV and likely to require Dedicated or Private - they care about data residency and SLA.
[00:50] Lena: RetailCo wants a VPC or on-prem option, right? they're regulated and will push for KMS/HSM and SOC2 evidence.
[00:58] Carlos: correct, RetailCo's ask will likely push them towards Redwood Private. We should propose a hybrid approach: Dedicated cluster for predictable throughput and then Private for any data-in-residence requirements. There's also the option of Dedicated with customer-managed key integrations (KMS) - fewer blocker items than full on-prem.
[01:15] Aaron: ok, and who will own the pilot? Vector or Redwood? we typically prefer partner-run pilots but can support co-led if Redwood SE is needed for perf runs.
[01:25] Maya: I think co-led for RetailCo and FinCorp - Vector handles the customer relationship and Redwood SE supports the benchmarking and perf tuning. For the three smaller deals we can do partner-led with Redwood as escalation.
[01:36] Sofia: timeline wise RetailCo wants a POC in May, FinCorp is targeting a June decision. Does that align with Redwood's capacity?
[01:44] Carlos: capacity-wise, yes - we have Dedicated pools we can reserve, but it depends on the exact throughput. For perf we need sample prompt sets and expected RPS and seq lengths. If RetailCo's seqs are long, we may need different kernel paths / quantization profiles.
[02:00] Aaron: i'll share sample payloads. question on cost: Vector is worried about token cost and latency tradeoffs - can you give a ballpark for a 2k token seq on a high-throughput retail inference?
[02:11] Carlos: ballpark, for a production setup using our curated medium LLM variant, with batching and prefix caching, you could be looking at X tokens / second economics - uh, rough estimate is 0.8 to 1.5 cents per 1k tokens depending on batching and KV cache hit rates. these numbers vary - we'll run a formal estimate once we have sample traffic.
[02:33] Lena: good, and on the commercials side, we need clarity on co-sell credit % and MQA attribution. Vector's legal also wants standard partner addendum - any model for that?
[02:44] Maya: our standard co-sell credit is 15% for active partner-sourced deals, higher band for strategic named accounts we both pursue (we can escalate to 20%). we'll put the exact language in an addendum. we also have a partner registration form to lock deal protection.
[02:56] Sofia: ok please send the partner registration link.
[03:00] Maya: will do.
[03:02] Carlos: technical question from our side, for HealthSys (medical charts use case), do they require PHI handling and specific encryption at rest?
[03:10] Aaron: yes, PHI concerns, they'd prefer Private deployment or a VPC with strict audit logs. also want SSO/SAML + RBAC baked in.
[03:19] Carlos: good to know - Redwood Private supports SSO/SAML and KMS integrations, and our console has token-level auditing that can be exported for SOC audits. we'll share a doc that outlines the controls. note: sometimes in quick conversations the product name gets jumbled - you'll see references to RedwoodDedicated or Redwood Infrence in notes, but it's the same platform.
[03:41] Maya: i'm noting that as a doc share item. back to pipeline: RetailCo - who is next touch?
[03:47] Lena: Vector has an intro scheduled next Tuesday but we need Redwood to join.
[03:52] Maya: Carlos can be on the call, we'll demo the flow and discuss pilot scope.
[03:57] Carlos: on the demo i'll bring a small perf run and show latency profiles - expect some jitter in a demo environment, production numbers will be better.
[04:05] Aaron: for the joint GTM, can we co-brand a one-pager? Vector marketing wants that for their AE motion.
[04:12] Maya: yes, we'll share a co-branded GTM one-pager and a joint case study template.
[04:18] Sofia: perfect. also, how do we handle lead routing and deal registration? we want a simple CRM handoff.
[04:24] Maya: typical flow is partner registers the deal in our partner portal, we assign an AE, then we tag it in the pipeline sheet and we agree on next steps. Sofia, if you share the pipeline sheet we'll label owners.
[04:35] Sofia: uploading now - ok it's in the shared drive.
[04:38] Maya: pulled it, I see the six opps, i'm updating owners: RetailCo -> Vector (lead), Redwood support; FinCorp -> Redwood (co-lead), HealthSys -> Vector lead with Redwood SE support.
[04:50] Lena: can we also mark the likelihood and next milestone? that helps prioritize co-sell resources.
[04:55] Carlos: yes please add milestone columns - demo scheduled, pilot scope, security review, PO.
[05:02] Aaron: one technical concern: RetailCo may require lower latency than normal, sub-200ms p99 for short responses. can Redwood meet that on Dedicated?
[05:10] Carlos: sub-200ms p99 for short responses is achievable with a tuned Dedicated config and aggressive batching limits; we may need to sacrifice some batching efficiency which increases unit cost. We'll provide a tradeoff table.
[05:22] Maya: i'll add that to the notes for the RetailCo pilot.
[05:25] Lena: legal - we need to see SOC2 report and a sample partner addendum.
[05:31] Maya: we'll send SOC2 and the partner addendum - expect that in the doc share.
[05:36] Carlos: also, small FYI: for benchmark runs we sometimes use quantized model variants to reduce cost; however for certain accuracy-sensitive prompts clients want full-fp or higher precision. We'll note the quality tradeoffs.
[05:50] Aaron: do we have a standard approach for joint references / case study credits? Vector wants to do a co-marketing webinar if RetailCo goes live.
[05:58] Maya: absolutely, we often do co-marketing and can commit to a joint webinar as a milestone once customer reaches X usage and revenue thresholds - we'll draft a co-marketing plan.
[06:08] Sofia: ok next steps and owners?
[06:12] Maya: action items: i'll send the joint GTM deck and pricing by next Monday 4/27; Carlos will run a quick perf checklist and sample latency/cost estimate for RetailCo and FinCorp by 4/28; Sofia will keep the pipeline updated; Lena will confirm partner registration and legal contact.
[06:27] Aaron: that timeline works from Vector side.
[06:30] Carlos: quick note - for the perf checklist i'll need sample prompt sets, expected concurrency, and any required compliance constraints (PHI). Aaron, can you share those by EOD Friday?
[06:41] Aaron: yes i'll send them today.
[06:43] Maya: great, anything else on commercials?
[06:46] Lena: one last ask - can Redwood be flexible on co-sell credit for two named strategic accounts? we want 20% instead of the standard 15.
[06:55] Maya: we can approve 20% for named strategic accounts pending RevOps approval; i'll escalate and confirm by 4/27.
[07:05] Sofia: noted.
[07:08] Maya: ok final recap: docs to share (SOC2, partner addendum, co-branded GTM deck), Carlos to do perf estimates, schedule joint demo next Tuesday for RetailCo, partner registration by Lena.
[07:21] Aaron: thanks all, we'll follow up in the pipeline sheet and get you the prompt sets.
[07:27] Maya: thanks everyone, talk soon.
